messages:
Amelia: Hey team, customer XA-908 reporting credits refilled but their app still gets 429s. They say credits showed +50% then dropped to 0 within minutes. Can someone look?
Devon: @Amelia can you share the org id and approximate time they noticed it?
Amelia: org-908, noticed at ~2026-03-17 00:05 UTC. They claim web UI showed 600 -> 900 tokens then back to 0.
Jordan: that sounds like a partial recharge race with long-running streaming requests. Any streaming sessions open at the time?
Amelia: customer sent a screenshot of websocket logs, includes: `HTTP 200 refill`, then `HTTP 429`, then `balance: 0`.
BillingBot: Automated notice: manual adjustment detected for org-908 at 00:04:23 UTC (operator: Priya). Change: +300 tokens temporary grant.
Devon: ah — there was a manual grant by @Priya for a different incident earlier. If grant was added to cached view but not fully reconciled with live usage counters it could show briefly.
Priya: Confirm I added a one-off grant while investigating a separate API error. I issued `grant_tokens(org-908,300)` at 00:04:23 UTC. I thought reconciliation job would do final commit.
Jordan: Looks like race: streaming RPCs holding long-lived token consumption counters weren't checkpointed; reconciliation rolled forward then immediate background aggregator subtracted usage from inflight sessions, taking the visible balance to 0. Repro hypothesis: grant + inflight KV cache leads to transient UI increase, then immediate counter consolidation reveals exhaustion.
Amelia: Customer insists they hadn't been using streaming at scale — they show only a few requests. Is there a way to get per-request IDs or a short audit trail so we can show them what consumed tokens?
Devon: We can pull usage events from the token-aggregator logs: query `SELECT * FROM token_events WHERE org='org-908' AND ts BETWEEN 00:00 AND 00:10` — I'll run and paste sanitized rows.
Devon: (pasted rows) `event:request, user:u123, tokens:250, ts:00:03:59`, `event:request, user:u124, tokens:320, ts:00:04:01`, `event:grant, operator:Priya, tokens:+300, ts:00:04:23`, `event:aggregation, reconcile, delta:-870, ts:00:04:30`
Amelia: That reconcile delta looks huge — why -870?
Jordan: The aggregator occasionally applies a negative delta when it detects unaccounted streaming consumption from ephemeral workers that didn't flush counters. In this case it appears two requests used ~570 tokens and aggregator also retroactively subtracted additional buffer tokens.
Priya: I can reverse the manual adjustment while we investigate, but we should also surface a clearer timeline to the customer.
Devon: Actionables: 1) I'll export the token_events slice and redact user IDs for customer. 2) Jordan, can you check streaming-worker flush logic around 00:03-00:05 UTC for org-908? 3) Priya, hold on reverse grant until we confirm with customer.
Jordan: FYI, I already found a streaming-worker restart at 00:03:57 on host gw-12 that caused KV cache to drop before checkpoint; that triggers the aggregator compensation.
Amelia: Good catch. I'll draft a response to the customer: explain transient UI + reconciliation behavior, include redacted events and propose a one-off credit while we harden the flush path.
Priya: I'll queue a reversible grant of +900 tokens in case customer wants immediate remediation, mark it as reversible in notes.
Devon: One more note — this edge-case only happens when manual grants occur while there are inflight uncheckpointed streams. Let's add a short doc blurb for support runbook.
Amelia: Agreed. I'll handle the customer message and the runbook draft. Thanks all :thumbsup:
BillingBot: Audit log entry created for reversible grant by Priya at 00:06:11 UTC (id: adj-20260317-001).
